comment: Ep98 USA vs Belgium (Play-Offs) — theme 'THE RED DEVIL AND THE TALISMAN'. Belgium = the Red Devils (Rode Duivels / Diables Rouges), a real, documented football nickname first given to the Belgian national team by the Belgian press in 1906 for their all-red kit and fiery style of play. USA = the Stars and Stripes, carried by the American Eagle (already carded as Legend 086 — referenced here as flavor only, not re-carded). OUR PREDICTION USA 2-1 Belgium (USA strike first through their young attack; Kevin De Bruyne, the Maestro, levels it 1-1; late, captain Christian Pulisic — the Talisman — strikes the winner). Legend 098 = The Red Devil, Belgium's Diables Rouges (Belgium). Squads: USA Pulisic(10,c)/Weah(21)/Balogun(9)/McKennie(8)/Adams(4); BELGIUM De Bruyne(7,c)/Lukaku(9)/Doku(11)/Tielemans(8)/Onana(4) — both sides run 5 named showcases, no squad-accuracy omissions needed this episode. Name-sync onsets match showcase clip starts (Pulisic/Weah/Balogun/McKennie/Adams at 55.5/60.3/65.1/69.9/74.7; De Bruyne/Lukaku/Doku/Tielemans/Onana at 90.6/95.08/99.56/104.04/108.52).

lines.text: In nineteen-oh-six, a Belgian newspaperman watched this team play with such fire that he gave them a name that never left them: the Red Devils.
And across the Atlantic, a different fire burns — America, the Eagle, all pace and belief, never afraid of the biggest stage.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends — episode ninety-eight. USA, versus Belgium. A play-off. Win, or the dream dies.
USA arrive with a golden generation hitting its prime. Belgium arrive as a fading golden generation, still hungry for one more famous night.
USA — the Stars and Stripes. Built around a captain who never stops believing, and a wave of pace up front.
Christian Pulisic, the captain — the Talisman, the man USA always trust to find a moment from nothing.
Timothy Weah is the winger, the pace down the flank that pins a back line in place.
Folarin Balogun is the finisher, the instinct in the box that punishes any mistake.
Weston McKennie is the engine, box to box, never stopping, never afraid of a tackle.
And Tyler Adams is the anchor, the shield in front of the back four, reading every danger first.
Belgium — the Red Devils. A golden generation, still built around the finest passer of his generation.
Kevin De Bruyne, the captain — the Maestro, still one of the best passers the game has ever seen, even now.
Romelu Lukaku is the hammer, the target man built to punish any square yard of space he's given.
Jérémy Doku is the flash, a dribbler who turns a one-on-one into pure fear for a defender.
Youri Tielemans is the conductor, the calm range-finder pulling every string in midfield.
And Amadou Onana is the wall, all size and timing, snuffing out danger before it starts.
So here is the riddle. Does the Red Devil burn brighter than the Talisman? Or does America's golden generation finally have its night?
And stay with me — because this one turns, late, on a single moment of magic.
Here is how we see it. USA come out sharp, hunting the game's first true opening.
The Stars and Stripes surge down the flank, quick and direct, and the Belgian back line is stretched thin.
And it lands! USA strike first — the young attack finds a way through, and their bench erupts.
Belgium need an answer, and there is only one man they trust to find it. De Bruyne goes hunting for the equaliser.
And De Bruyne finds it! One-one. The Maestro, exactly when Belgium need him most.
But USA want more. Late, the Talisman senses the moment, and the whole stadium holds its breath.
Pulisic strikes! Two-one, USA. The captain, exactly when it matters most.
Two-one USA. Belgium were brave and the Maestro nearly held them level, but the Talisman found one flash too many.
Our prediction — USA two, Belgium one. Pulisic, late. Not played yet — the real ninety is yours to watch.
And Belgium leave with their heads high — the Red Devils, still one of the most dangerous sides left in this tournament.
USA march on. The Stars and Stripes, a golden generation finally delivering on the biggest stage.
So you tell me — the Red Devil, or the Talisman? Comment BELGIUM for the Red Devils — comment USA for the Stars and Stripes.
They say the fire never left them — the Red Devils, the name a newspaperman gave them in nineteen-oh-six, and never took back.
The players write the night. But the Red Devil carries one truth — the fire that gave them their name still burns, whatever the scoreline.
Here is how. Go to worldcup twenty-six dot world and create your free account — ten seconds, and the Red Devil, Legend zero-nine-eight, is yours.
Then pick three of the forty-eight nations, and every goal they score, scores for you. Free to play, just for glory.
So sign up tonight, claim your Legend, and send this to a friend who loves the beautiful game. Hit like, hit subscribe, and I'll see you at the next one.
